question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Long in the tooth

options.text: Killing of a certain ethnic or religious group on a massive scale
To be old, often too old to do something
Be optimistic, even difficult times will lead to better days
The show has come to an end

solution:
The correct answer is **"To be old, often too old to do something."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expression "**long in the tooth**" is an idiom that is often used to describe someone who is old or aging. (अभिव्यक्ति "long in the tooth" एक मुहावरा है जिसका उपयोग अक्सर किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति का वर्णन करने के लिए किया जाता है जो बूढ़ा हो या उम्रदराज़ हो।)

 
 
• **Example**: Even though he's a seasoned programmer, some might say he's getting a bit*** long in the tooth***__ in the rapidly evolving tech industry.
 
 
 
• It's a figurative way of referring to the fact that as horses age, their gums recede, making their teeth appear longer.
 
• Therefore, when someone says another person is "long in the tooth," they are suggesting that the individual is getting older.
 
• It's a lighthearted or humorous way to talk about aging, and it's commonly used in informal contexts.
 
• Hence, option **2** is the correct answer
